Elliot — thanks for the data and flag. We're actively investigating. Quick summary from initial telemetry:
- We are seeing queue depth and token processing time increase in the us-west dedicated GPU pool serving BeaconPay's reserved slot.
- A small subset of our host kernels hit an unexpected contention path after a model change on 06/17 (non-invasive weight layout tweak); this increases per-token CPU/GPU sync cost under certain batch shapes.
- As a result, overall pool throughput dropped ~28% starting ~07:40 PT; autoscaling hasn't been able to reclaim headroom fast enough for the peak.

Immediate steps we're taking (ops + infra):
1) Marcus is rolling a quick kernel fallback to yesterday's runtime to remove the contention path (ETA 22m).
2) We're enabling priority routing for your reservation so queued requests prefer your dedicated instances (5–10m).
3) Tessa is warming prefix cache nodes for your high-frequency tokens and prepopulating KV entries where possible.

We can also provision a limited burst allocation from shared pool for the next 2 hours if that helps short-term while we complete the rollback. Marcus — can you confirm the rollback plan and impact window?

Sofia
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Quick technical note — rollback plan and risks:
- Plan: revert kernel selector to v20270616 (last known good) on the affected CUDA host group. This removes the recent layout optimization that appears to trigger the contention on batch-1024 shapes.
- Impact: each host will be drained, updated, and brought back online; expected per-host downtime ~90s but we will drain traffic gracefully so user RPCs will flow to other hosts.
- Scope: starts immediately after approval; estimate 18 hosts in the us-west pool; phasing to minimize disruption.
- Risk: if queue depth spikes as we drain, tail latency could temporarily increase for small windows — mitigation by prioritized routing and burst allocation.

I'll coordinate withEdge Autoscaler to pull ~1200 qps capacity from shared pool in 5 minutes after rollback starts.

Marcus
SRE, Serving Runtime
